title: Learning programs
statement: For a dimension $n\in\mathbb{N}$, an access mode (random-example access or membership-query access), and an output type, a learning program may return a value, draw an unbiased random bit, draw one or a batch of independent uniform labeled examples, draw a batch of uniform cube inputs, or draw a finite matrix of independent uniform labeled examples. It may also compute a pure output from such a matrix with an explicitly specified local-work charge, query the target at a chosen cube input, or charge a specified number of local computation steps; the random-example and query operations are available only with their respective access modes.
hypotheses_covered: access mode is random-example access or membership-query access
matrix operations use a finite index set
batch sizes and local-work charges are natural numbers
